'''Brandon Sam Bass''' (born April 30, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU Tigers]] and was selected in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[New Orleans Hornets]]. Bass played 12 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the Hornets, [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Orlando Magic]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He finished his career in 2020 after three seasons with the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]] in China.

== Early life ==
Bass was born in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]], the oldest of three siblings; he has a brother, Chris, and sister, Dashia. Bass is the son of Charles Joseph and Aretha Bass. Bass was raised by his mother until her death. When he was 10 years old, he witnessed his mother die from a heart attack. Bass and his siblings subsequently moved in with their father but due to not feeling comfortable at their father's home, Bass and his siblings moved in with their aunt, Estelle.<ref name=herald>[http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/celtics_nba/boston_celtics/2013/11/brandon_bass_just_wants_to_be_best_dad_he_can_be Brandon Bass just wants to be best dad he can be]</ref> While at his aunt's house, Bass was living with his siblings and five of his aunt's children. It wasn't until he was 13 years old that Bass began playing basketball competitively.<ref>[http://www.brandonbass30.com/foundation Brandon Bass Foundation] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150213055934/http://www.brandonbass30.com/foundation |date=February 13, 2015 }}</ref>

== High school career ==
Bass attended Capitol High School in Baton Rouge where he began gaining recognition for his play. By his senior year in 2002–03, he was ranked the seventh best power forward in the nation, the 11th best overall player in the nation, and the third best player in the Southeast by Rivals.com.

While in high school, Bass had a GPA of 2.7 with an ACT score of 17. He graduated as a part of the class of 2003. He received interest from Connecticut, LSU, Mississippi St., Cincinnati, Kentucky, Miami (FL), and USC to join their basketball programs. Of those schools, Bass received offers from Connecticut, LSU, Mississippi St, and USC, ultimately deciding on attending LSU.

Bass also received many honors while in high school, being named a part of the [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] team, EA Sports Roundball Classic Roster, and the McDonald's All-America Game.<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/ocsn/basketball/recruiting/player-Brandon-Bass-8998 Brandon Bass – Yahoo! Sports]</ref> Bass finished the McDonald's All-America Game with 14 points and 3 assists.<ref name=realgm>[http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Brandon-Bass/Summary/126 Brandon Bass Player Profile – RealGM]</ref> While on the McDonald's All-American Team, Bass played alongside the likes of future NBA superstars such as [[LeBron James]] and [[Chris Paul]].

==College career==
Bass joined the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]] basketball team in 2003 and played for them until 2005. In his first year at LSU, Bass played 29 games, starting in all of them. As a freshman, Bass averaged 12.8 points, 7.4 rebounds, 1.9 blocks, in 34.9 minutes per game. In his second season, Bass played and started in 30 games, averaging 17.3 points, 9.1 rebounds, 1.6 blocks, and 33.6 minutes per game.

Bass received numerous honors while playing at LSU. In 2004, he was named a part of the SEC All-Freshman Team and was also named the SEC Freshman of the Year. In 2005, Bass was named a part of the SEC All-Tournament Team, First Team All-SEC (Coaches), SEC Player of the Year (Associated Press), and the SEC Player of the Year (Coaches).

Bass' career-high in points in college was 30 points in a game against Louisiana-Lafayette on November 21, 2004. He achieved his college career-high in rebounds with 17 against Mississippi State on February 16, 2005. He achieved his career-high in blocks with six on two separate occasions with his last one being in Houston on December 21, 2004. His career-high in minutes was 45, which came against Ohio State on January 15, 2005.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Brandon-Bass/Bests/126/NCAA Brandon Bass Career Bests]</ref>

Bass left LSU after his sophomore year, choosing instead to declare for the [[2005 NBA draft]]. He ended his college career with career averages of 15.1 points, 8.3 rebounds, 1.8 blocks, and 34.3 minutes per game. He started and played in a total of 59 games.<ref name="realgm" />

==Professional career==

===New Orleans Hornets (2005–2007)===
Bass was drafted in the 2005 NBA draft by the [[New Orleans Hornets]], being taken with the 33rd overall pick. On August 24, 2005, Bass signed a multi-year contract with the Hornets.

In his first season in the league, the Hornets twice assigned Bass to their [[NBA Development League]] affiliate, [[Tulsa 66ers]]. He ended up only playing one game in the D-League, scoring 16 points, along with 5 rebounds and 2 blocks.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/nbdl/players/b/bassbr01d.html Brandon Bass D-League Stats]</ref>

In his time with the New Orleans Hornets, Bass averaged 2.2 points, 2.2 rebounds, 0.2 blocks, and 8.6 minutes per game. He played a total of 50 games, having started in 4 of them.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bassbr01.html Brandon Bass NBA Stats]</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2007–2009)===
On July 26, 2007, Bass signed a two-year deal with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2007_08/ |title=Transactions: 2007–08 Season |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2015-02-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150531052916/http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2007_08/ |archive-date=2015-05-31 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 1, 2009, Bass made a turnaround jumper to give [[Jason Kidd]] his 10,000th career [[Assist (basketball)|assist]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2009/news/03/01/kidd.assists.ap/index.html Mavs' Kidd reaches 10,000 assists milestone against Raptors] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140527212449/http://www.nba.com/2009/news/03/01/kidd.assists.ap/index.html |date=2014-05-27 }}</ref> In two seasons for Mavericks, he averaged 8.4 points and 4.5 rebounds in 160 games.

===Orlando Magic (2009–2011)===
On July 10, 2009, Bass signed a four-year deal with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web | last = Aldridge | first = David | title = Forward Bass agrees to four-year deal with Magic | url = http://www.nba.com/2009/news/features/david_aldridge/07/10/magic.bass/ | work = NBA.com | date = July 10, 2009 | access-date = February 4, 2015 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150707230555/http://www.nba.com/2009/news/features/david_aldridge/07/10/magic.bass/ | archive-date = July 7, 2015 }}</ref> In two seasons for the Magic, he averaged 9.1 points and 4.4 rebounds in 126 games.

===Boston Celtics (2011–2015)===
[[File:Brandon Bass 2012.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Bass with Boston in 2012]]
On December 12, 2011, Bass was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Glen Davis (basketball)|Glen Davis]] and [[Von Wafer]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press121211-celtics-acquire-bass.html Celtics Acquire Bass]</ref> In his first regular season game for the Celtics on December 25, 2011, he recorded 20 points and 11 rebounds in a 104–106 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=311225018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111226201240/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=311225018|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 26, 2011|title=Knicks need every ounce of Carmelo Anthony's 37 in win over Celtics|work=ESPN.com|date=December 25, 2011|access-date=February 4, 2015}}</ref> On May 21, 2012, Bass tallied a playoff career-high 27 points to help the Celtics gain a 3–2 series lead over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Fenton|first=Jim|url=http://www.tauntongazette.com/sports/x1040012640/CELTICS-NOTEBOOK-Brandon-Bass-has-best-playoff-game-of-his-career|title=CELTICS NOTEBOOK: Brandon Bass has best playoff game of his career|work=TauntonGazette.com|date=May 22, 2012|access-date=May 22, 2012}}</ref> The Celtics won that series, but were eliminated in the next round by the [[Miami Heat]]. In the 2011–12 season, Bass established his career-high points average to 12.5 and his rebounds to 6.2 that increased the Celtics' offense and defense.

On July 14, 2012, Bass re-signed with the Celtics.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/071412-celtics-resign-brandon-bass.html Celtics Re-Sign Brandon Bass]</ref>

In January 2015, Bass re-gained his starting spot and finished the season averaging 10.6 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bassbr01/gamelog/2015/ Brandon Bass 2014–15 Game Log]</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2015–2016)===
On July 9, 2015, Bass signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/150709_brandonBass|title=Lakers Sign Brandon Bass|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2015|access-date=July 9, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Lakers in the team's season opener against the Minnesota Timberwolves on October 28, recording 2 points and 6 rebounds in a 112–111 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Wolves edge Lakers 112–111 in first game since Flip's death|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151026213514/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 26, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 20, 2016, he scored a season-high 18 points in a loss to the Sacramento Kings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160120/SACLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Cousins' 36 points lead Kings past Lakers again, 112–93|work=NBA.com|date=January 20, 2016|access-date=January 21, 2016}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2016–2017)===
On July 19, 2016, Bass signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/laclippers-sign-brandon-bass |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160722054057/http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/laclippers-sign-brandon-bass |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 22, 2016 |title=LA CLIPPERS SIGN BRANDON BASS |work=NBA.com |date=July 19, 2016 |access-date=July 19, 2016 }}</ref> For the season he appeared in 52 games, averaging 5.6 points in 11.1 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Gary Washburn |title=It's been a difficult two years for Brandon Bass. So he's trying to reinvent himself |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/celtics/2017/07/29/been-difficult-two-years-for-brandon-bass-trying-reinvent-himself/5oUUZ5WNVUfMNZIwS9CvXP/story.html |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=[[Boston Globe]] |date=29 July 2017}}</ref>

===Liaoning Flying Leopards (2017–2020)===
In August 2017, Bass signed with the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Arthur Hill |title=Brandon Bass To Play In China |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2017/08/brandon-bass-to-play-in-china.html |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=hoopsrumors.com |date=17 August 2017}}</ref> Due to restrictions on international travel, Bass along with teammate [[Lance Stephenson]] were unable to return to China in June 2020 to finish the 2019–20 season with the team.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Lu Hui |title=Liaoning activate American guard Mayo for future CBA matches |url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-06/21/c_139155875.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809220651/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-06/21/c_139155875.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 9, 2020 |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=xinhuanet.com |date=21 June 2020}}</ref>

==National team career==
In February 2021, Bass was selected to the 14-player roster for the final round of the [[2022 FIBA AmeriCup qualification]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Isaiah Thomas, Joe Johnson headline U.S. roster for AmeriCup qualifying |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/02/03/isaiah-thomas-joe-johnson-headline-u-s-roster-for-americup-qualifying/ |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=3 February 2021}}</ref> On 19 February he scored 12 points in a 93–77 victory over [[Bahamas men's national basketball team|Bahamas]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Sam Quinn |title=Isaiah Thomas, Joe Johnson combine for 30 points in Team USA victory over the Bahamas in FIBA AmeriCup |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/isaiah-thomas-joe-johnson-combine-for-30-points-in-team-usa-victory-over-the-bahamas-in-fiba-americup/ |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=20 February 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bass' younger brother, Chris, played [[college basketball]] for Louisiana State as well.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=1522546 |title=#4 Chris Bass |access-date=2010-03-29 |archive-date=2012-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020114630/http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=1522546 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
An avid hip-hop fan, Bass has been writing rap songs since he was 11 and recording them since he was 16. The main topic he chooses to address in his music is his upbringing and overall life.<ref>[http://www.xxlmag.com/news/2014/12/brandon-bass-hip-hop-junkie-interview/ NBA Player Brandon Bass On Writing Raps And His Love For No Limit]</ref> Bass is married to  Melissa Prejean. The couple has one son, Brandon Jr., and one daughter, Bella.<ref name="herald" />
